A century after extinction in Ireland, majestic sea eagles are soaring back into the ecological record books. 🦅🌿

Once Gone From Ireland, Majestic Sea Eagles Continue Their Comeback with Rare New Chick
Evidence: historical restoration, conservation success, thriving wildlife. #Conservation #Ireland

Fota Wildlife Park announced the successful birth and fledging of a white-tailed sea eagle chick—the first in over a decade—marking a milestone in Ireland's decades-long raptor reintroduction program.

Field reports and wildlife officials confirm over 200 eagles released since 2007 have established a self-sustaining Irish population, restoring top-tier avian predators to coastal habitats successfully.

White-tailed sea eagles vanished from Ireland over a century ago due to human persecution. In 2007, conservation agencies began reintroducing Norwegian eagles, resulting in a self-sustaining wild population today.
